title: Inference Time Optimization with Confidence Dynamics
claim: A scalar signal is computed by contrasting aggregated values from the start and end of a sequence.
layout: 2 rows: bin strip on top, head/tail formulas feeding a central result box
description: A wide, short diagram with two rows. The top row, labeled 'Trace Bins:', is a horizontal strip split into three blocks. On the left is a yellow 'First P% tokens' block. The middle is a large gray 'Middle bins (not used in CDG)' block. On the right is a green 'Last P% tokens' block. The bottom row has three rounded boxes. On the left is a yellow 'Head Bin' box with the formula for mean head confidence, which averages per-token confidence over the head positions. On the right is a green 'Tail Bin' box with the matching tail formula. In the center is a blue box titled 'Confidence Dynamic Gain', with ΔC = tail minus head. A brown arrow marked '−' runs from the head box to the center box. A green arrow marked '+' runs from the tail box to the center box. Color coding ties each bin to its formula. The eye goes first to the blue central box.
caption: Confidence Dynamic Gain (CDG) computation, i.e., $\Delta C_{\ell}$. Each trace with $T$ tokens is partitioned into $N$ position-normalized bins. The head bin confidence $\bar{C}_{\ell}^{head}$ averages over the first $P%$ of positions, and the tail bin confidence $\bar{C}_{\ell}^{tail}$ averages over the last $P%$. The CDG $\Delta C_{\ell}$ captures how confidence evolves from reasoning start to conclusion.
abstract: Inference time optimization techniques, such as repeated sampling, have significantly advanced the reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs). However, the critical role of model uncertainty remains largely underexplored in these optimization strategies. In this paper, we investigate the dynamics of confidence along reasoning trajectories and for first time reveal a surprising and unique pattern: correct answer traces tend to exhibit confidence improvement over time (positive confidence gain), while incorrect traces show attenuated or declining confidence as reasoning proceeds. Based on this observation, we propose Confidence Dynamic Gain (CDG) based voting, which incorporates how the confidence trajectory of the response evolves along the reasoning chain. Experiments across four open-source architectures (DeepSeek-R1, gpt-oss, Gemma-3, Qwen-QwQ) on the AIME24/25, HMMT25, and BRUMO25 benchmarks demonstrate that CDG yields a significant performance boost over baselines. These results demonstrate that our method provides a robust discriminative signal for improving answer selection in LLM reasoning. We also provide theoretical insights for this phenomenon. Code will be released at https://github.com/Accenture/CDG.git.
